- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often fails to anticipate further decline; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price increases; apply 1–3% upward adjustment to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive, model lags; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and apply gradual ramp-up.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 3–5 day highs; use 10-day rolling mean as baseline for correction if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), model tends to over-smooth; use 7-day exponential smoothing with sentiment-weighted decay.
